## Context
Cut L1b of the shape of basicly-1dpggot (Orchestrator decisions 2026-11-20). Criteria 1 and 2 of the epic. orch lesson add records a scope (local or basicly) and, for a basicly-scope lesson, an origin. No consumer repository name is recorded; the reproduction command must stand alone. The refusal reuses the existing rules, one rule in one place: MACHINE_PATH_RULES and ABSOLUTE_PATH_RULE in .basicly/core/kit/tracker/redact.py, and identity_pattern() with the machine-username rule in .basicly/core/hooks/tracker-path-scan.py, including its configured-holder exemption (basicly-5v1rrl9). Host names stay uncovered, because no rule for them exists.
payload.title: Record a scope and an origin on each lesson and refuse a machine path or user name

payload.name: description
payload.value:
## Context
When basicly finds a learning in a consumer repository, I want it to flow back to the main basicly repository with its evidence, so every installation improves the harness.

## Owner intent
2026-11-17, relayed by the Orchestrator in his words: "basicly must be able to learn and self-improve - if it is happening in a client repo, then it must know how to bring back the learning to the main basilcy repo, for example by creating a PR."

## Shape
Shaped with the Orchestrator on 2026-11-20. A consumer recognises a learning only from a recorded fact: a repeated hook or gate refusal (counted by orch errors), a person's correction, or a basicly command that fails or refuses wrongly. A lesson is basicly-scope only when its fix changes a file that basicly install writes; only those are exported. A lesson records no consumer repository name. It closes only by a commit on the default branch of the named checkout. Cuts: .1 shape (this), L1b scope and origin, .2 verified close, .3 orch errors in the kit, .4 export to basicly, .5 pull request.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
Every outcome of install, init, link and migrate prints its result on the first line and "next: COMMAND" on the last; a refusal prints "refused: REASON" and "fix: EXACT COMMAND".
In a git repository, init installs the skills and creates a local vault in the user state folder, named by its genesis commit, and the committed .basicly-tracker.toml holds no absolute path.
When init finds an existing ledger, issues.jsonl, br or beans source, it creates the vault, does not attach, and names migrate as the next command; outside a git repository it installs the skills and names the repository step.
A vault moved before this change, whose toml names its URL, still resolves to its existing clone.
--version prints the package version, and init is listed in the top-level --help.
init --scope project writes instruction files only with --with-instructions.
init sets the project prefix from the repository or folder name, shows it, and names --prefix to change it, so the first create needs no config step.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
migrate removes the git user.name, user.email, the "Full Name <email>" form, the login name, host names and home paths by default, --redact-name takes several values, and it refuses to publish unless a personal-data scan finds zero.
migrate validates the source schema and size before any write, previews by default, publishes only with --yes, and keeps no private map unless --private-map FILE is given.
migrate deletes the derived caches before the freeze, commits the freeze, and attaches only after counts and digests match.
A second migrate after success prints "already migrated" and exits 0; several sources are listed and refused with the next command.
The supported beads export format and version are named in the README and checked on import, refusing an unknown format by name.
After an import, the result names the imported prefix and the ledger prefix and how new records are numbered.
After migrate, the result names the files to commit and says whether .beads/ stays, and a commit of the migration passes the claim gate.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
The README opens with the four commands and their first output lines, a table of each state with its message and next command, and a section per agent.
A CI job runs one fixture per state (no git, no remote, existing ledger, issues.jsonl, failed push, second run), a localhost ssh bare repository and a synthetic issues.jsonl with a zero personal-data scan, within 5 minutes.
The install command pins a released version, and the package, the ledger pin and --version show one version number.
The README shows the full local life cycle (create with --field issue_type=task, review and confirm with exact evidence JSON, claim .basicly/ledger ID, close), and every example uses basicly-tracker.
The README starts with the local mode and says when to choose a vault.
The CI test of the first-time flow (terminal baseline 2026-11-20: 160 s, 4 unexpected failures) runs in under 60 s with zero unexpected failures.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
migrate maps each beads issue to a short-form task (issue_type task) with its title, description, status, priority, labels and edges, so it is ready at once unless it lacks a title.
After importing a beads backlog, tracker ready lists every open imported record that has a title (terminal baseline 2026-11-20: 0 of 19 ready, 19 in refine).
